rowType.description: "rate" (a published rate for a date and currency) or "conversion" (an amount converted to ILS).

ok.description: true when a rate was found (and, for conversions, the amount converted); false for a free notice row.

reasonCode.description: OK, UNKNOWN_CURRENCY, INVALID_AMOUNT, INVALID_DATE, DATE_IN_FUTURE, INVALID_CONVERSION, NO_RATE_PUBLISHED, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_FORMAT_ERROR or INTERNAL_ERROR.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation, including which day's rate was used when it differs from the requested date.

position.description: Conversion rows: 1-based position in the input "conversions" list.

reference.description: Conversion rows: the caller's own reference (for example an invoice number), echoed back.

date.description: The calendar date asked for (YYYY-MM-DD). Echoed as written when a conversion date could not be parsed; null for an unknown-currency notice in a range.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (or the text that could not be recognised).

rate.description: Rate rows: the published representative rate, ILS per `unit` units of the currency.

rateUsed.description: Conversion rows: the published rate applied, ILS per `unit` units of the currency.

unit.description: Units of the foreign currency covered by the rate (1 for most, 100 for JPY).

change.description: Rate rows: percent change against the previous published rate; null when unknown.

amount.description: Conversion rows: the amount in the foreign currency.

ilsAmount.description: Conversion rows: amount x rate / unit in ILS, rounded half-up to 2 decimals.

rateDate.description: The publication date of the rate that was used (equals `date` on publication days).

daysBack.description: Days between `date` and `rateDate` (0 when the rate was published on the requested date).

publishedAt.description: ISO timestamp of publication when the source states it, otherwise null.

provisional.description: true while the rate may still be revised (about 15 minutes after publication).

dataSource.description: "live" (Bank of Israel) or "fixtures" (synthetic test data; only possible outside the Apify platform).
